A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Virne NFV-RA benchmark. Their complete main texts and appendices support comparison, including readable equations, tables, and figures. Relocated analyses and renumbered figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations comparing RL and traditional algorithms, implementation ablations, and generalization, solvability, and scalability evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds training-curve comparisons and evaluations of safe-RL and meta-RL variants.

M1.justification: v2 adds evaluated safe-RL and meta-RL augmentations of PPO-DualGAT, involving constraint-cost optimization and task-specific policy adaptation (Appendix C.2; Figure 13). These extend training options while retaining the core simulator, sequential placement/routing procedure, and base architectures.

E1.justification: The evaluated topologies and scenarios remain WX100, WX500, GEANT, BRAIN, heterogeneous resources, latency constraints, and varying traffic, demands, and network sizes. The new training comparisons use retained coverage. Partial observability and noisy resources are discussed as extensions, not newly evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: Figure 4 newly compares PG-DualGAT and A3C-DualGAT against PPO-DualGAT. Figure 13 adds safe-RL and meta-RL variants to a comparison with basic PPO-DualGAT. Comparator membership in the existing benchmark tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The new training-algorithm experiment holds the DualGAT architecture fixed and measures R2C across training simulations. Existing simulation distributions, training budgets, and testing settings are retained. Appendix C.6 adds protocol specifications, but its acceptance-based solvability definition conflicts with the retained R2C evaluation rather than establishing an actual metric replacement.

E4.justification: Figure 4 adds learning-dynamics analyses for training algorithms, reward choices, and features; Figure 13 examines safe-RL and meta-RL augmentations. Existing generalization, offline solvability, and scalability analyses remain. The solvability analysis moves into Section 4.3 rather than being newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix D.1.1 in both versions specifies ten testing seeds, 0, 1111, through 9999, and random seed initialization during training. No new confidence intervals, significance tests, uncertainty bands, or repeated-run reporting practices are introduced.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 2, 3, 8, and 9 and the retained experimental plots are unchanged. New Figure 4 reports superior PPO learning performance relative to PG and A3C. Figure 13 reports improvements from meta-RL and safe-RL augmentations, with safe RL leading the displayed comparisons.

T1.justification: The previously skeletal Appendix C.2 gains formal multi-task meta-learning and constrained-MDP objectives, and C.6 adds evaluation definitions. Appendix A.1 also reverses the flow-balance terms, from v1 Equation 6 to v2 Equation 5, without consistently updating their summation indices. The basic allocation objective remains unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a customizable NFV-RA benchmark integrating over 30 algorithms, modular RL implementations, practical evaluation perspectives, and empirical guidance. Separating evaluation into its own contribution bullet and strengthening descriptive wording do not materially change these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretations concerning topology density, resource efficiency versus revenue, and failures of decoupled placement/routing heuristics. New Appendix F explicitly identifies flow-level abstraction, global observability, and deterministic resource allocation as deployment limitations. These add substantive applicability boundaries absent from v1.

D1.justification: New Appendix C.4 and Figures 7–8 provide actionable module descriptions, configuration flags, and class-extension examples; C.7 supplies documentation access information. v2 also discloses default virtual-node ordering and the reusable constraint flag. These substantially expand implementation guidance, while existing hyperparameters and hardware specifications remain stable.

R1.justification: v2 adds nine cited works, broadens discussion of allocation, scaling, and migration, and adds three studies to the related-work survey in Table 4. The central positioning against fragmented NFV-RA benchmarks remains unchanged. The safe-RL reference's publication update is not a new work.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution list are rewritten, experimental interpretations are extensively revised, and offline solvability moves from Appendix D.3 into the main narrative. The appendices gain a substantially expanded explanatory structure, dedicated limitations, and additional manuscript statements. Title, authorship, headings, and citation style also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 4, 7, 8, and 13, updates the pipeline illustration, and expands Table 4. The original solvability heatmap becomes a smaller main-text Figure 5. Conference formatting and author-year citations also reshape the layout; retained experimental plots preserve their underlying data.

improvement.justification: The added training comparisons better support methodological choices, while the customization guide and explicit simulation limitations improve usability and transparency. These gains are tempered by inconsistencies in the new protocol description: C.6 defines solvability through acceptance while Figure 5 measures R2C, and the revised flow-balance equation has mismatched summation indices. Overall, the additions provide a modest net improvement.
